contentBlocks.text: You've learned three poetic tools — ਲੈਅ, ਬਿੰਬ, ਉਪਮਾ. Today: a specific traditional form that uses all three in just two lines.

ਦੋਹਾ is a traditional short poetic form built from two ਤੁਕ (lines) that work together to express one complete thought — often something reflective or wise, expressed compactly. Because it's so short, every word has to earn its place: a strong ਦੋਹਾ usually uses a clear ਬਿੰਬ (image) and steady ਲੈਅ (rhythm) rather than trying to say too much. Read this example structure: line one sets up an image or situation, line two delivers the thought or turn that completes it. Try writing your own two-line ਦੋਹਾ about something you've observed in everyday life — keep it short and let one strong image carry the meaning.

Writing within a tight two-line form is real practice in choosing words carefully — a skill that makes longer poems stronger too. Tomorrow you'll write a complete original poem combining everything from this week.

objectives: Describe ਦੋਹਾ as a traditional two-line poetic form expressing one complete thought
Write an original two-line ਦੋਹਾ using a clear image
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's three tools: ਲੈਅ, ਬਿੰਬ, ਉਪਮਾ.
2. Introduce ਦੋਹਾ's two-line structure (setup line, then a completing thought).
3. Model writing one example ਦੋਹਾ together.
4. Have the child write their own.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: writing a complete original poem.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child write their setup line and completing-thought line as two separate sentences first, then tighten them into a more poetic two lines
Ready for more: ask them to revise their ਦੋਹਾ to include a simile from Day 2, not just an image
The value of this exercise is brevity — resist letting the child expand it into more than two lines
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. A ਦੋਹਾ is a traditional two-line poetic form expressing one complete thought. 2. Line one typically sets up an image or situation; line two delivers the completing thought. 3. A strong ਦੋਹਾ uses a clear image and steady rhythm rather than trying to say too much in a short space.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'Punjabi literary history, poetry, and formal writing' description by introducing a real traditional poetic form, applying the week's rhythm/imagery tools within a specific structural constraint.
